canon.resumen: What the show depicts, with nothing changed.
canon.explicacion: The hive can’t kill or harm any form of life, not even a plant: it doesn’t harvest, fish or slaughter animals. It eats what was already stored, fruit that falls on its own, animals that die naturally and the HDP from humans who die. It releases livestock and pets, keeps milking the cows, and everyone eats what they need until the food runs out. The Joining is in July, the month with the least stored grain of the year; the canon’s clues point to late spring or summer.

cena.resumen: From day one, the ration implied by Cena’s video: ~67%.
cena.explicacion: In the episode 6 video, John Cena says someone his size needs eight 300-kcal cartons a day: 2,400 kcal. But Cena weighs about 114 kg, and a body like that burns close to 3,000, so that diet is already a deficit of ~21 kcal per kilo. Scaled to an average person, it comes to ~67% of what they need. Here the hive hands out that fixed ration from day one: the food lasts longer, but those who were already thin start dying early.

estirar.nombre: The hive stretches food to 10 years
estirar.resumen: They ration so the food lasts Koumba’s ten years.
estirar.explicacion: Koumba tells Carol that, according to the hive itself, most people will starve to death within the next ten years. Here the hive plans ahead: each day it works out the ration that would make the stored food, plus what will keep coming in (fruit, HDP, meat, milk), last the full ten years, never dropping below 60% of what’s needed. Everyone eats less from the start, so hunger comes sooner for the most vulnerable, but the overall collapse is delayed.

diciembre.resumen: Right after the northern harvest: full granaries.
diciembre.explicacion: The canon doesn’t say when the Joining happened, and the world’s stored grain varies a lot with the harvest calendar: there are ~1,385 million tonnes on July 1 and ~2,185 on December 1. With the Joining in December, the hive starts out with about 200 more days of food. Everything else is the same as canon.

ganado.resumen: The animals aren’t released: they eat the same grain as people.
ganado.explicacion: In the show, the hive releases the livestock: Kusimayu’s fellow villagers set theirs free when they join. Here, so as not to let the animals starve, the hive keeps feeding them as before. But livestock today eat ~1,100 million tonnes of cereal a year, more than people eat directly, so the stored food lasts half as long (from ~589 to ~288 days). In exchange, more animals die on farms and their meat is put to better use.

resquicios.resumen: Generous readings of the rule: births, eggs, honey and grain from dead plants.
resquicios.explicacion: The rule is not to kill or harm, but some things might fit within it: letting livestock keep giving birth so the milk never runs out, collecting eggs and honey (to that end, the hive keeps feeding the livestock), gathering grain from crops that were already planted once the plant dies on its own at maturity (70% of what would have been harvested) and, from the second year on, sowing and gathering only once the plant has dried up (50% of a normal harvest). It isn’t canon: in the video, Cena says they can’t harvest wheat or corn or rice. It shows that the problem is the rules, not the food.
